To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the α-Fe 2O3/vermiculites materials with higher specific surfaces areas, a smaller crystal size and structural defects that a play crucial roles in photocatalytic activities, are obtained at the lower calcination temperature (500 °C).
the photocatalytic activity of α-Fe 2O3 and its composite with vermiculite clay material depends on the specific surface area, crystallite size and oxygen vacancies in the structure.

the α-Fe 2O3 nanoparticles with higher specific surface area, a smaller crystalline size, and structural defects that play a crucial role in photocatatalytic activity, can be obtained by using vermiculite clay as a carrier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach of the preparation of a new photocatalytic material, which can be used as an efficient and cost-effective catalyst for the reduction of CO2 to hydrocarbon fuels.
the synthesis and characterization of a novel α-Fe2 O3/vermiculites material with high photocatalytic activity.
the synthesis, characterization, optical and photocatlytic properties of the α-FeO3 nanoparticles/Ver material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the α-FeO3/Ver material prepared at 500 °C is the most efficient photocatalyst for the reduction of CO2.
the α-FeO3/Ver material prepared at 500 °C is a promising photocatalyst for the photocatalytic reduction CO2.
the α-Fe 2O3/ Ver material prepared at the calcination temperature of α-Fe 1O 3/ Ver material at 500 °C has the best photocatalytic activity for reduction of CO2 to CH4 and H2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the photocatalytic activity of the α-Fe 2O3/vermiculites is higher than that of pure α-Fe2О3 and it depends on the specific surface area, crystallite size, structural defects and optical properties of the material.
the α-Fe 2O 3/vermiculites with the highest surface area (BET), the lowest crystallite size and the highest concentration of oxygen vacancies are the most active photocatalysts for CO 2 reduction.

the higher specific surface area, a lower crystallite size, a higher number of oxygen vacancies and the lower band-gap energy (1.98 eV) of α-FeO3/Ver (T = 500 °C) material are responsible for the highest photocatalytic reduction activity of CO2 to methane (CH4).
The main takeaway from our work is that
α-Fe2/Ver materials prepared at lower calcination temperature (500 °C) are more efficient in photocatalytic reduction CO2 to methane than those prepared at 700 °C.
α-Fe2/Ver materials prepared at 500 °C have better structural, textural and optical properties, and consequently better photocatalytic activity.
the α-Fe 2O 3 nanoparticles/vermiculte clay material with the highest photocatalytic activity for CO2 reduction can be obtained by calcination of the α-Fe(OH)3/Ver material at 500 °C.
